Born and raised in North Vancouver, Jim Hanson is seeking his fourth term on District Council. Jim is married to Ruth Hanson, and together they have two adult children. Jim is a practicing lawyer. If re-elected, Jim will commit to relentlessly pursuing transportation initiatives to relieve congestion, such as his idea to pave a third lane on the Cut eastbound between Lynn Valley Road and Mountain Highway, to separate North Vancouver residents from highway/bridge traffic. He will support investments in transit and active transportation. On housing, Jim will support development that addresses the needs of District residents (social, supportive, seniors and rental housing near transit hubs) and will not vote for large, expensive, strata development. Jim commits to only voting for tax increases that are at or below inflation. Jim will speak out loudly for accountability from Metro Vancouver for the North Shore Waste Water Treatment plant debacle and advocate for governance reform at Metro. Jim has served on a variety of boards and committees, including the Policing Committee, Library Board, Heritage Committee, and the Advisory Committee on Disability Issues. Jim Chairs the North Shore Standing Committee on Substance Use.

dnv-council-kyle-aidan.name: Aidan Kyle
dnv-council-kyle-aidan.text:
Residents deserve leadership that listens, communicates clearly, and is accountable. That means better transparency, stronger communications, and engagement that works for everyone, including the younger residents like myself who will inherit the decisions we make today.

I was raised in North Vancouver, went to school here, met my wife here, and I'm now lucky enough to be raising our daughter here. I came up in the film industry and work in industry relations today. I'm running for Council because I want DNV to be for her what it's been for us.

I want to be a voice for the future of our community. Future generations should be able to stay, put down roots and build a life here. That means tackling housing costs, congestion and infrastructure together to plan for the community we’re becoming.

dnv-council-mann-kulvir.name: Kulvir Mann
dnv-council-mann-kulvir.text:
My experiences as a trustee, volunteer, parent, and resident—have given me the opportunity to listen to people from across our community, understand different perspectives, build relationships, and work collaboratively toward practical solutions. They have also reinforced my belief that our community is strongest when we work together. I am committed to helping build a District of North Vancouver that remains a safe, inclusive, vibrant place to live—one where residents can access the programs, services, and opportunities they need, and where people are proud to call home.

I will listen carefully, ask questions, work collaboratively, and make thoughtful decisions in the best interests of District residents. I have 8 years as a trustee so know how the governance and budget process works - DNV is $300M while the NVSD $260M. I have been volunteering and done community service for over 20 years. I sit on 5 boards - NVDPL, NSDRC, PHT, NS Safety Council and NV Band & Strings Parent Association and a variety of committees across the north shore. I have built great meaningful relationships and trust in the community during this time and believe I would be a great representative on DNV Council to speak on behalf of residents and have their voices heard. We need council to be seen and active to represent us. Find alternate ways to get funding to support residents.

dnv-council-munro-linda.name: Linda Munro
dnv-council-munro-linda.text:
Linda Munro is a community-driven leader and a trusted voice in North Vancouver. With more than two decades of experience in communications, public affairs, and community engagement, she has built her career on strengthening relationships, solving complex challenges, and ensuring people feel heard. First elected as a School Trustee in 2021—and topping the polls in both of her campaigns—Linda has worked tirelessly to improve access to quality public education. As a trustee, she acts as liaison to facilitate communication between community members and the school district. As Board Chair from 2023 to 2025, she helped guide district policy, supported families and educators, delivered leadership for trustees, and championed initiatives that put students at the centre of decision-making. Linda’s professional background includes senior public affairs roles at Capilano University, where she led external communications, government relations, and issues management. She has also represented major organizations locally and internationally, including Doctors of BC, World Vision in the Asia Pacific region, and global PR agencies in Vancouver and London. A long-time volunteer and community builder, Linda has served in leadership roles with local schools, libraries, youth organizations, and community service groups. She currently volunteers with Family Services of the North Shore and the Strachan Hartley Legacy Foundation. Linda, her husband Scott, and their two teenagers call Lynn Valley home. She holds a Master of Arts degree in Journalism from Western University, Bachelor of Arts degrees in Political Studies and Geography from Queen’s University, and a Certificate in Non-Profit Management from Simon Fraser University. She brings a strong commitment to public service, and experience, integrity, and a collaborative approach to every role she takes on—and she is dedicated to representing and strengthening the community she calls home.

I want the District of North Vancouver to be where people of all generations find community connections, opportunities for economic development and a place to thrive.

dnv-council-muri-lisa.name: Lisa Muri
dnv-council-muri-lisa.text:
I feel grateful that the community has placed their trust in me over these many years. Other than being a mother, it has been the most important work I have ever had the privilege of being involved in. Over the last 15 years this community has seen much change, creating new communities for families, while protecting the single family neighborhoods that we love. As we continued to advance redevelopment, I believe we did not focus as we should have on the impacts of change. Traffic congestion has many contributors, internal movement, neighbouring growth, expansion of industry, the volume of cars driving through to the Island, Coast and Sea to Sky, and quite simply the over capacity of the bridges. In this very challenging economic time, we need to pivot, focus on clear control of spending, lowering tax’s to address the uncertainty of the NSWWTP, assess the impact of change on the natural environment, and focus on maintaining our current house before we continue to expand. The future is uncertain, we need to move cautiously and make responsible decisions. The Official Community Plan is meant to be a living document, subject to change, and yet it has been implemented with a focus on fast approval of redevelopment above anything else. The plan envisioned a complete sustainable community, but it has not delivered the services, infrastructure, protection of the environment, or the sustainable financial means to support it. We have used development to pay for things, and now the tap has been turned off and we are wondering how will we move forward. The community has experienced unprecedented growth, not just in the District, but all over the North Shore and the region. Traffic congestion, taxes, jobs, affordability, have all contributed to anxiety about what we are doing.....and now the uncertainty of our economy amid the worlds challenges raise the stress of “can we afford it”? I believe we need the benefits of growth, but we need to pace ourselves and catch up with our infrastructure. We need to co ordinate with our neighbors and hold control over our zoning in order to manage the impact of change. We have alot of work in front of us. I am experienced and passionate about this place I grew up in..... I respectfully ask for your continued support on October 17 2026. Thank you!

To challenge the status quo, it bring corporate historical knowledge to the Council table, to speak up for the community!

dnv-council-nwabuisi-victoria.name: Victoria Nwabuisi
dnv-council-nwabuisi-victoria.text:
I love the District for its natural beauty, strong neighbourhoods, and—most of all—its sense of community. I’m running for Council because I want to help prepare thoughtfully for the future while preserving what makes North Vancouver feel like home. Through my work in finance and education, as well as volunteering locally and internationally, I’ve learned the importance of listening, bringing people together, and making thoughtful decisions. When I’m not working or volunteering, you’ll find me reading the North Shore News, running with my group from North Shore Sports Medicine, or discovering a new trail or park with family and friends. I’m proud to call the District of North Vancouver home, and I’m excited about what we can build together for generations to come.

North Vancouver is changing. I believe we can embrace that change while preserving what makes this community feel like home. We can do better. We can be: thoughtful about growth, creative about affordability, and intentional about building a connected community. I’m ready to listen, speak up, and help shape a North Vancouver where everyone has a place. Progress and preservation don’t have to be opposites. I love how Tamara Edgar of the Beacon Community Newspaper puts it when she says: “We don’t have to become something entirely different. We simply have to remain open to becoming more fully what we are capable of becoming.”

dnv-council-pope-catherine.name: Catherine Pope
dnv-council-pope-catherine.text:
Catherine Pope is a District of North Vancouver Councillor and former investigative journalist who has spent her career asking tough questions on behalf of the public. Born and raised on the North Shore, Catherine came home after a career that took her across Canada and the UK. Two decades as an investigative journalist with Global TV taught her to follow the facts and hold decision-makers to account. She brings the same approach to Council. Catherine led the call for a public inquiry into the massive cost overruns at the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant. Council unanimously endorsed her motion, making the District the first municipality in Metro Vancouver to back an inquiry. She continues to fight for lower utility costs for NS taxpayers and change at Metro Van. Since her election in 2022, Catherine has helped deliver more affordable housing, a new toddler playground, new pickleball courts and expanded recreation, safer streets, youth-centre funding and greater transparency in Council decision-making. To tackle traffic congestion, she's pushing for a new bridge, SkyTrain, more transit and active transportation routes. Above all, she's working to keep the North Shore affordable for seniors, families, young people and workers. Catherine served 20 years on the Victoria Foundation's Adoption and Permanency Committee and was on the board of the Disability Foundation. She champions youth mental health services and volunteered with school PACs and the NS homeless count. Away from Council, she's a mom, pickleball player, e-bike rider, pet lover.

I love this commmunity and want to continue working to make it an even better place to live! Strong voices are needed this term as we fight for lower utility bills, infrastructure funding to fix congestion and afffordable homes.

dnv-council-wilson-stephanie.name: Stephanie Wilson
dnv-council-wilson-stephanie.text: I know a brighter future is possible. I know we can lift those who need a hand, grow in harmony with each other and with the land, and build a more resilient future together. I’ve worked in the mental health and substance use sector for 17 years. I see first-hand how systems can change lives. When people have stable housing, food in the fridge, and neighbours that care, they also have hope. What does a brighter future look like? Truly affordable housing. We’re relying on for-profit systems to solve problems created by profits. Governments have an obligation to collaborate and build non-profit and co-op housing. Building renters into the conversation. The number of renters in the District is growing, and many people (like me!) see renting as a long-term option rather than a temporary stopover. Renters need an advocate and they need to be part of decision-making. Fast and reliable public transportation. We can’t simply pave our way out of traffic congestion. Expanding the transit network with RapidBus and Bus Rapid Transit creates real alternatives to driving. I don’t own a car and primarily use transit to get around, so I know just how many neighbourhoods aren’t served well. Spaces for connection. Improving access to libraries, parks, recreation, sports, and cultural opportunities for everyone. Climate justice. Protecting our land, air, and water from a perspective of equity. I’m proud to be endorsed by the Vancouver and District Labour Council and CUPE 389. I’m a union member and I continue to support the workers that keep our communities running.

dnv-council-boyd-daina.name: Daina Boyd
dnv-council-boyd-daina.text: I grew up on the North Shore and raised my family in the Seymour area, where I still live today. As a renter who commutes daily by transit across the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge, I understand firsthand the challenges many residents face, including traffic congestion, the impacts of growth and development, and the shortage of attainable housing. These are complex challenges that won’t be solved by one person or one council alone. They require collaboration among residents, businesses and all levels of government, and the decisions we make today will shape our community for generations. That perspective shapes my approach. With more than 30 years of experience in both the public and private sectors, I have developed a proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships across all sectors of the community. I am particularly passionate about addressing affordable housing, homelessness, traffic congestion, and ensuring that the pace of development reflects the needs and priorities of the residents who live here. I care deeply about this community and don’t take for granted how fortunate we are to live here. Preserving what we value takes commitment. My approach is simple: work together, build on our achievements, and remain open to learning from one another. That’s how we move our community forward. If elected, I will work tirelessly on your behalf. I encourage everyone to vote on October 17 and to choose candidates who understand and share your concerns.

dnv-council-mah-herman.name: Herman Mah
dnv-council-mah-herman.text: Herman Mah and his family have called the District of North Vancouver “home” for 25 years. His focus is “Family + Community” so that the District continues to be a great place to live and work. Herman brings a diverse background to Council. He graduated from UBC with a business degree. Professionally, he oversaw the BCIT downtown campus, administered real estate projects at BC Housing and managed affordable housing for a non-profit. Herman has volunteered for many community groups for over 40 years. He was Treasurer for the Pemberton Heights Community Association, volunteered on DNV’s Community Services Advisory Committee and coached for North Shore Girls Soccer Club. Herman recently joined the board of Canadian Mental Health Association on the North Shore. Herman’s work and volunteer experience enables him to be a thoughtful leader who brings a balanced approach to address issues faced by our community while managing the financial issues. If re-elected, Herman’s priorities include (1) addressing traffic, congestion and infrastructure needs by advocating to senior levels of government for funding for transit, mobility lanes and a new crossing, (2) supporting local economy by streamlining application processes and (3) advancing affordable housing with a strong sense of community. This can be achieved by investing in co-op housing, easing guidelines for coach houses and focusing majority of growth in town centres that are connected with transit. There is a lot of work ahead for the next Council and, together, I want a bright future for generations to come.

dnv-trustee-branston-jennifer.name: Jennifer Branston
dnv-trustee-branston-jennifer.text:
Why I Care About Public Education Public education matters to me because it has the power to shape opportunities, build confidence, and create a sense of belonging for every child. As a parent of a student who recently graduated from the North Vancouver School District in June 2026, and as a community volunteer, I have seen firsthand the important role schools play in students’ lives. Schools are more than places of learning. They are communities where young people discover their strengths, develop friendships, explore new interests, and gain the skills they need to navigate the world. My involvement in education has also shown me the incredible impact that dedicated teachers, support staff, administrators, and volunteers have on students every day. Their commitment helps create learning environments where students can grow academically, socially and emotionally. What inspires me most is the belief that every student deserves the opportunity to succeed. While every learner’s journey is different, all students benefit when families, educators, and communities work together in support of their learning and well being. Through my work with Parent Advisory Councils and through my District level engagement, I have come to appreciate how important it is to actively listen to students and families, foster collaboration, and build strong relationships across our school communities. These experiences have strengthened my commitment to supporting a public education system that serves students and families with care, respect, and accountability. At its heart, my passion for public education comes from a simple belief: When we invest in students, we invest in the future of our communities. If elected as a North Vancouver School Board Trustee, my focus will be simple: Putting students and families first. I want every student to feel supported, inspired, and confident about their future. I will champion mental health, student and staff well being and safe, inclusive schools where every learner has a sense of belonging, and feels they have the support they need to succeed, I am committed to providing strong support for students with diverse learning and support needs and for meaningful learning opportunities for all students, ensuring educational equity and opportunity for all. I will promote and model fiscal responsibility, student centered leadership, good governance principles, and greater transparency in decision making. I will support technology and future ready learning, expanding career and skilled trades opportunities, and support strengthening partnerships among schools, families, and the broader community.

I am Jennifer Branston, a community advocate, volunteer, operations and governance professional, and former Chair of the North Vancouver District Parent Advisory Council (NVPAC) (DPAC). For the past eight years, I have worked alongside students, families, educators, school leaders, and community partners to strengthen inclusive education in the North Vancouver School District. Through this work, I have helped remove barriers and expand access to meaningful educational opportunities for all learners. I have also supported both Families and Parent Advisory Councils (PACs) in navigating the policies, processes, and procedures of the North Vancouver School District (SD44), helping to ensure they are informed, engaged, and empowered to contribute meaningfully at both the school and district levels. I bring 10 years of sustained, hands on experience with the North Vancouver School District. As a parent and partner group representative, I have served on committees focused on Policy Review, Inclusion, Accessibility, Emergency Preparedness, and more. I have attended every School Board meeting, in person or online, and contributed directly to policy development on several subcommittees. I understand both the importance of good governance and the value of listening to the people our decisions affect. Throughout my years of service at the school and school district level, I have seen firsthand what is possible when we listen to one another, work collaboratively, and keep student success and well being at the heart of every decision. With experience in both operations and governance, including my current role as Operations & Governance Coordinator for Canada’s National Autism Network and years of service on non-profit boards, I bring a clear understanding of where governance ends and operations begin, and of the responsibilities trustees carry in providing thoughtful, accountable leadership. I believe strong schools are built on partnership, transparency, inclusion, and accountability. Every student deserves the opportunity to learn, grow and belong in a welcoming, supportive, and inclusive learning environment. I am still committed to fostering strong, connected school communities where families are recognized as essential partners in education; Indigenous peoples, students, and staff feel heard, valued, and respected; and decisions are made with care, transparency, and a shared sense of purpose. I truly believe that, together, we can continue building schools where every student feels a genuine sense of belonging and has every opportunity to succeed. My focus remains on collaboration, transparency, and supporting the needs of students, families, and educators throughout our school community. I invite you to learn more about my experience, my priorities, and my commitment to public education by visiting my website, Facebook page, by email or phone call. If you see me around town, please do not hesitate to say hello, some of the most meaningful conversations happen when you least expect them. I hope to earn your trust and support, and I would be truly grateful for the opportunity to continue serving and giving back to the community we all share and care so deeply about. I look forward to connecting with you! Jennifer Branston

For many years, the North Vancouver school community has been an incredibly important part of my life. My years of experience as the Chair of NVPAC gave me the opportunity to listen to families, work alongside educators and district staff, advocate for students, and deepen my understanding of both the strengths of our public education system and the very real challenges experienced by those at the heart of our schools. I have seen meaningful progress, particularly in inclusive education and support for neurodivergent learners, and that gives me hope. I also know there is still more we can do to ensure every student and family feels seen, heard, valued and supported. It would mean a great deal to me to continue giving back to this community as a School Board Trustee, bringing my experience, care, and commitment to working collaboratively toward schools where every learner is welcomed, supported and knows they truly belong.

dnv-trustee-charrois-michael.name: Michael Charrois
dnv-trustee-charrois-michael.text:
I am a professional actor, a proud member of Canadian Actors' Equity Association, Union of BC Performers and the Alliance of Canadian Cinema Television and Radio Artists. For the past five years I have been working on the front line as a Constituency Advisor in the North Vancouver- Seymour MLA community office. I am also a member of BCGEU Local 703. In addition to the clerical and administrative business skills I use in the office, I have also used my love of life-long learning to develop diverse performance skills (juggling, magic, public speaking, balloon animal twisting, clowning, writing, producing, directing and teaching) to maintain a fullfilling artistic career on stage, screens, and on the street. For a complete list of my screen credits visit imdb.com. Born and raised in Edmonton, I attended Victoria Composite High School's performing arts program and went on to study acting and playwright at the Banff School of Fine Arts and the University of Alberta. Before I completed my degree, I was offered a job as resident actor at Stage Polaris. Five shows a year plus summer drama camps; it was a great gig. It was at the Stage Polaris Academy of Drama that I started teaching drama classes in 1986. Starting with juggling workshops, moving onto acting classes and directing student productions, teaching has always been a way for me to stay active and in the profession in addition to performance engagements. At the turn of the century, I moved to Vancouver. I taught drama classes at the Burr Theatre, Vancouver School Board Continuing Education and Evergreen Arts in Coquitlam. At the Evergreen, I was performing arts education coordinator, tasked with developing and selling arts education programs, curriculum, development, and facilitating performing arts workshops for SD 43 Pro D days. I currently teach adult improvisation and film/television acting at Evergreen Arts and I take my Storytelling Through Drama Games Workshop into school classrooms in SD 43 and 42. I will be teaching clowning and magic for kids and adult drama at Christine Sinclair/ Shadbolt community programs later this fall. I have recently been performing physical theatre (juggling/magic) for the Arts Club Education program. I believe the purpose of primary and secondary education is to teach empathy through diversity, secularism and inclusion. Curiosity, creativity, and a questioning mind, are some of the skills that the arts in education (and science) promote.

I've worked in the MLA's office for the past five years. I know that a big part of the job of an elected official is to listen to concerns, direct constituents to the appropriate place or person and know where and how to use connections and appropriate pressure to try to resolve problems. This is the role I would assume if elected to be a school board trustee.

dnv-trustee-gerlach-cyndi.name: Cyndi Gerlach
dnv-trustee-gerlach-cyndi.text:
I grew up in North Vancouver and raised my three children here. I’ve served as School Trustee since 2011, including as Chair and Vice-Chair. My work on DNV committees and with provincial and national organizations reflects my commitment to public education, inclusion and community. My involvement in public education began long before I became a trustee. As a parent, community advocate and volunteer, I learned the importance of listening to the people most affected by decisions and ensuring their voices are part of the conversation. Over the years, my community involvement has extended beyond the school board through work with District of North Vancouver committees and provincial and national organizations focused on education, accessibility, disability inclusion and governance. These experiences have given me a broader perspective on the important connections between schools, families, local government and community partners. One of the things I value most about serving as a trustee is hearing directly from students, families, staff and community members. I have been told many times that people appreciate that I listen and bring their concerns forward, even when I may not agree with them. To me, that is an important part of representative leadership. After four terms, I bring significant experience to the Board, but I don't believe experience means having all the answers. It means knowing the questions to ask, understanding how to move issues forward, and continuing to listen, learn and improve. Public education has shaped my life, my family and the community I grew up in. I remain deeply committed to ensuring our public schools are places where every student has the opportunity to learn, belong and succeed.

Public education is constantly evolving, and our schools need to respond to the diversity of students in today's classrooms. We need to strengthen literacy and numeracy, ensure students feel they belong, support different ways of learning, and advocate for provincial funding that gives students and staff the resources and supports they need. After four terms, I bring significant experience to the role, but I don't believe experience means having all the answers. It means knowing the questions to ask, understanding how to move issues forward, and being willing to speak up when something needs attention. I also believe representation begins with listening. Students, families, staff and community members need to know their voices matter. I may not always agree with every concern brought to me, but I will listen, ask questions and bring those concerns forward. I am running again because I care deeply about public education and believe I can continue to make a meaningful contribution to North Vancouver's students, schools and community.

dnv-trustee-haines-rob.name: Rob Haines
dnv-trustee-haines-rob.text:
I have worked as a secondary classroom teacher, primary special education teacher, International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme educator, and Vice Principal. I've taught in Ontario to Hong Kong and British Columbia, giving me a broad perspective on different educational systems, approaches to learning, and the needs of students and school communities. These experiences have allowed me to understand education from many perspectives. As a classroom teacher, I supported students through their academic and personal development. In special education, I worked with students with diverse learning needs and saw the importance of providing the right support for every learner. Through the IB program, I focused on high educational standards and preparing students for future success. As a Vice Principal, I worked alongside students, families, educators, and support staff to help lead a school community. I believe strong school leadership starts with listening, collaboration, and a clear focus on student success. I am committed to advocating for students, supporting educators and staff, and strengthening public education in North Vancouver. I bring more than two decades of practical experience, a commitment to inclusive and high-quality education, and a strong belief in the role public schools play in building healthy, connected communities.

I believe we need to strengthen support without lowering expectations. As a Trustee, I will bring my experience as an educator and school leader to advocate for students, invest in strong public schools, and help ensure the resources students and educators need reach our classrooms.

dnv-trustee-khan-raheela.name: Raheela Khan
dnv-trustee-khan-raheela.text:
Finance to purpose-led leadership in equity & financial literacy: Yale World Fellow & Oxford alumna (dual MBAs). My promise to SD44: apply proven governance to deliver a future-ready, inclusive education system where every child is safe, valued, belongs, & is equipped to succeed.

My story is one of transition from finance to purpose, and from metrics to meaning. For a long time, my world revolved around numbers managing financial portfolios, markets, and performance. I transitioned into leadership development and social impact work because I believe real growth happens when systems are designed with people at the centre. Driven by that conviction, my career is now focused on youth empowerment advocating for financial capability as a life skill, cultural democracy, inclusive growth and equity-focused initiatives that benefit our communities and economy alike. Youth are the heart of a resilient community, and public education is the single most important public service we have. I am running not just because of my background, but because I am deeply passionate about youth development, and all of my current work directly aligns with the responsibilities of a School Trustee. As a Lynn Valley mother of two children in elementary school, my commitment to this community is deeply personal. Beyond my hands-on volunteer work and active school engagement, I hold a strong educational foundation as a Yale World Fellow and Oxford alumna with dual Master’s degrees in Business Administration and Information Systems. I bring analytical rigor, strategic vision, and a deep financial understanding of how taxpayer dollars are managed. As a board leader, volunteer, and advocate for early-childhood financial literacy, I have spent years building bridges across cultures and generations. My priority is helping young people build essential life skills, confidence, and resilience to thrive in an ever-changing world all through human-centered governance that supports students, families, and educators alike.

My focus is on bringing my experience as a school trustee to translate public resources, thoughtful governance and community priorities into meaningful, measurable impact for students and families in every classroom, ensuring future-readiness to thrive in an ever changing world

dnv-trustee-nickerson-laura.name: Laura Nickerson
dnv-trustee-nickerson-laura.text:
I’m running to be a school board trustee for the North Vancouver School District #44. I have a MA in Environmental Education and Communication, and I have spent my career helping people to connect with nature, with each other, and with the places they call home. My professional life has been rooted in community education, specifically outdoor, environmental, and sustainability learning. Including 5 years working in a school district, experiencing how important people are to the healthy functioning of the school system. I am an active volunteer. As a youth baseball coach with the North Shore Baseball Association where I get to support kids as they grow, learn, and build confidence through sport. And on my school’s PAC, where I focus on fun ways to encourage safe and active travel to and from school. I feel deeply connected to the North Shore. I’m a nature lover. You can find me and my family skiing in the winter, paddling in the summer, and on our bikes whenever we can. These experiences shape my values and my belief in the importance of community, stewardship, and creating opportunities for young people to thrive. I believe that curiosity strengthens community: when we listen to one another, ask questions, and stay open to learning we make better decisions together. This mindset shapes how I work, how I lead, and how I show up in my community.

Every day, students learn within ecosystems shaped by people, buildings, and policies; and their wellbeing depends on how well we steward these systems. I am committed to responsible, transparent oversight of district resources, ensuring that financial and physical investments directly support student learning. I believe that school districts should be leaders in our communities: open, inclusive, and welcoming to all learners and their families. Most importantly, I want our district to champion the voices of students. While not yet old enough to vote, their experiences, hopes, and challenges deserve to shape the decisions we make. I’m running to help steward a school district where every student can thrive, every family feels included, and every decision reflects our shared commitment to a strong public education system.

dnv-trustee-north-layne.name: Layne North
dnv-trustee-north-layne.text:
A life long resident with a background in AI Safety, Layne North is determined to bring to SD44 a perspective urgently needed but perpetually missing. A student through Covid and AI's emergence, he brings subsequent experience teaching about AI use and his generation's future

My struggle with the education system. begins at Highlands elementary, where I stayed until grade 5. I spent everyday reading at the back of the class, unchallenged and unengaged. I’d became withdrawn after intense bullying. I also had struggles with ADHD, which left me alternating between excitement at new information and immense boredom and distraction in a classroom that only let kids progress at one speed. The school system was unable to help with either of these problems. They didn’t have the resources or expertise. My parents felt they had no choice but to try a smaller private school at the time. But parents shouldn’t have to look away from public schools to find support for their children. Our schools should be able to support students with various needs and interests to get to where they need to go. To make sure they get the opportunities and education they need to thrive after graduation. That’s our job as School Board Trustees, and I’m determined to provide perspective and guidance on the board as the only candidate who’s been in the system in the last two decades.

dnv-trustee-tsiakos-george.name: George Tsiakos
dnv-trustee-tsiakos-george.text:
I am a parent, educator, librarian, and two-term North Vancouver School Trustee committed to strengthening public education and supporting student success. Since being elected in 2018, I have served on the North Vancouver Board of Education, including as Vice-Chair and Board Chair. In these roles, I have worked collaboratively with fellow trustees, students, families, staff, and community partners to advance student learning, well-being, and inclusion. Professionally, I serve as Interim Associate University Librarian, Collections at the University of British Columbia, where I provide strategic leadership for library collections and resources that support teaching, learning, and research. I am currently on secondment from my substantive role as Head of the UBC Law Library. I am also an Honorary Lecturer at the Peter A. Allard School of Law, where I teach legal research, writing, and analysis, and a course on Education and the Law. I hold degrees in history, law, and library and information studies from UBC and I am a non-practising member in good standing with the Law Society of British Columbia. My family and I have called North Vancouver home for many years. My wife is a lifelong North Vancouver resident, and together we are raising our two children in the community we are proud to call home. Throughout my career and community service, I have focused on bringing people together, listening respectfully to different perspectives, and working collaboratively to address challenges. These principles continue to guide my work as a trustee and my commitment to public education.

Serving as a School Trustee has been one of the most rewarding forms of public service I have undertaken. Over the past eight years, I have had the opportunity to work with students, families, staff, and community partners to support learning and strengthen public education in North Vancouver. I am seeking re-election because I believe there is still important work to do. Our schools continue to face growing and increasingly complex demands, and students need strong advocates who are committed to inclusive learning environments, well-being, and educational excellence. Drawing on my experience as a trustee, parent, educator, librarian, and university administrator, I will continue to approach decisions thoughtfully, collaboratively, and with students at the centre. My goal is simple: to help ensure that every student has the opportunity to learn, belong, and succeed.

dnv-trustee-boehm-mike.name: Mike Boehm
dnv-trustee-boehm-mike.text: My name is Mike Boehm and I am honored to be a candidate as a School Trustee in North Vancouver School District. I have been a North Vancouver District resident for close to 40 years and all four of our children were students with the School District in Elementary, French Immersion and High Schools. I have been actively involved in a number of organizations related to children including President of Highlands Little League, North Shore Girls Softball, Director of Canuck Place; previous Chair of North Vancouver Chamber of Commerce as well as Not For Profit organizations including Chair of North Shore Community Foundation and a current director of The Hollyburn Society. Over the years I have also coached various youth sports teams including baseball, softball, hockey and football. In May 2024 I was presented a District of North Vancouver Community Service token of appreciation. I am a firm believer of listening, open communication and collaboration and believe my skillset and experience developed over the years would be an asset to the School District at all levels namely administration, teachers and support staff, students and parents. I have long maintained in "giving back to the community to make our community better tomorrow than it was yesterday" and on Saturday October 17 I hope to receive your support. In my professional career, I was most recently Vice President, Business Development with KPMG

dnv-trustee-rinfret-ainslie.name: Ainslie Rinfret
dnv-trustee-rinfret-ainslie.text: I believe the school system is key to a strong community foundation and I want to help ensure ours is exceptional. Operational Expertise: My professional background is in finance, operations, and organizational efficiency. I have an eagle eye for unnecessary bottlenecks, and genuinely enjoy the process of untangling inefficiencies to improve processes and thoughtfully allocate resources. Personally Invested: With 4 young children in (or about to enter) the North Van public school system, I am personally committed to ensuring our schools provide excellent educational experiences in the long-term. I also have an up-close understanding of the realities families experience as they navigate the system. Community Experience: I have served on non-profit boards supporting children and volunteered with several community-based organizations on the north shore. I know what it looks like to work collaboratively, balance competing priorities, allocate limited resources, and make decisions in the best interests of the broader community. High Quality Education I want to help reduce the burden of inefficient processes and unnecessary administration so teachers and staff can maximize the time and energy they spend providing high quality educational experiences for our children. I was lucky to grow up in North Van and attend school in the district. School fairs, sports days, and family dances created happy memories as well as a strong sense of community. I want to give back by contributing to a strong, effective, and forward-looking public school system for the next generation.
